title: Scoped routing-retention-occupation theorem
statement: Retention has probability at least 1-eta. In almostSureWeak mode, the occupation-and-retention event also has probability at least 1-eta. In inProbabilityWeak mode, routed deviation probabilities tend to zero and, for every delta>0, full deviation probability is eventually at most eta+delta. The original survival-property constitutive margin is at least 1-eta.toReal in both modes.
assumptions: ["Certified source Exact GR, disjoint source and target regions, actual fixed-world admissible intervention, original comparison set, and infinite routing budget eta<=1.", "For almostSureWeak conclusions the target has that mode; for inProbabilityWeak conclusions the target has the declared test-integral in-probability mode, with each fixed bounded continuous test and positive deviation threshold. Grounded uniform PR separately requires eta<1 and all original grounding and confirmatory gates."]
proof: "Canonical restart, positive-mass arrival-law transport, and target invariance prove the shared retention bound. Finite-prefix deletion transports almost-sure occupation to the corresponding occupation-and-retention event. In the in-probability case, summing routed exit-time contributions makes routed deviations vanish, while the unrouted remainder leaves the eventual eta+delta budget. The original source-survival argument supplies the shared margin bound."
open: "Arbitrary custom convergence modes, eta=1 positive constitution, and arrival without target invariance are excluded."

title: Typed two-player response protocols and generic metric bounds
statement: Within the conditional-product two-player subclass, declared closed-loop and open-loop generators define admissible interventions retaining P. For two interventions of one frozen family and property, absolute effect difference is bounded by protocol gap, which is bounded by the sum of effects. A uniform gap G on the original comparison domain bounds the absolute difference of original margins by G. The strict-menu Boolean witness has closed-loop effect1, open-loop effect0, gap1; a separate correlated law cannot be represented by the conditional product.
assumptions: ["The typed two-player construction uses state-conditional product action laws and conditional product common/private update laws; it is a subclass, not a representation of all games. Shared-state-mediated correlation remains representable.", "Fix the world P, replacement, declared anchor menu, intervention family and metric-valued path property. Margin transport requires the gap bound at EVERY state of the SAME original comparison set.", "For the declared sufficient opponent-locked strict submenu, anchor action/update factor through own state and the allowed common coordinate, and the common update reads only its old common state. This exogenous-common condition is sufficient, not a general necessity characterization."]
proof: "Typed assembly and the admissible replacement cases preserve the literal world kernel. Metric triangle and reverse-triangle inequalities give pointwise bounds; uniform infimum comparison yields the margin bound. Exact canonical Boolean paths verify the strict witness, and a diagonal Boolean law rules out a universal product representation."
open: "These are protocol-relative metric bounds, not causal mediation or an ordering of closed/open effects. No global n-player generalization or strict MA2 witness is supplied."

title: Dual invariant-law and conditional occupation-margin bounds
statement: The implemented Lipschitz-dual distance obeys the invariant-law contraction budget; a Lipschitz descriptor and functional give the two-pair margin bound under all four explicit full-path factorization equalities.
assumptions: ["Probability laws invariant under the original and perturbed Markov kernels; the dual test class is bounded measurable real 1-Lipschitz functions, with a separate finite bound for each test and no shared supnorm-one cap.", "The encoded contraction sends any W1DualLE bound c to rho*c; every row has W1DualLE defect at most delta; 0<=rho<1; and hfin explicitly supplies a real c with W1DualLE(pi,pi-tilde,c). Both baseline and intervention bundles have these data.", "The chosen factorization map is measurable and L_h-Lipschitz; the functional satisfies the source IsW1LipschitzFunctional condition; all four full-path factorization equalities hold on the identical original comparison domain. The map is not inferred from either specification descriptor."]
proof: "Invariance, triangle, contraction, and defect transform a supplied finite bound c into rho*c+delta. With L=delta/(1-rho), induction gives W1DualLE at c_n=rho^n(c-L)+L. Since c_n tends to L, closedness of the universal test inequalities proves the final dual bound. Lipschitz pushforward and the functional bound control both value pairs, then metric triangles and uniform infimum comparison control the original margins."
open: "Coupling-W1 identification, primitive coupling certificates, and derivation of the four ergodic factorizations remain separate open bridges."

assumptions: ["Probability laws invariant under the original and perturbed Markov kernels; the dual test class is bounded measurable real 1-Lipschitz functions, with a separate finite bound for each test and no shared supnorm-one cap.", "The encoded contraction sends any W1DualLE bound c to rho*c; every row has W1DualLE defect at most delta; 0<=rho<1; and hfin explicitly supplies a real c with W1DualLE(pi,pi-tilde,c). Both baseline and intervention bundles have these data.", "The chosen factorization map is measurable and L_h-Lipschitz; the functional satisfies the source IsW1LipschitzFunctional condition; all four full-path factorization equalities hold on the identical original comparison domain. proof: "Invariance, triangle, contraction, and defect transform a supplied finite bound c into rho*c+delta. With L=delta/(1-rho), induction gives W1DualLE at c_n=rho^n(c-L)+L.
